questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Since my choices were very limited as my topic at KU had few collaborations, I just chose the warmest in EU. Bordeaux seemed fine and new, so would be fun.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The French system vs the danish school system/general attitude is not to be dealt with lightly. Be aware the cultural differences, language barriers !!! and where you are in life (socially/survival skills etc)

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Not one bit easy! If you choose Bordeaux be aware that there is very little help, chaos continuously and you are on your own. 
You learn by being there that no one knows anything and they don't care = you end up not caring and go with the flow of unknowingness.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was an introduction meeting, but since everyone had personal needs and questions, and concerns, it didn't really help.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Crous

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Either you had your own (I had) or you shared. The people who shared kitchens had homeless people use their facilities; the staff would not make them leave or call the police; water wouldn't work for days etc. Not great.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I wouldn't recommend crous; I payed 250 euro for 9kvm; the heating didn't work, my window was not sealed, everyone had bedbugs (even the renovated ones), no help, etc. My ceiling even had a big crack.
Spend more money on a shared apartment!!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Terrible, their website is a mess, and finding courses was such a tedious process. They have their own systems, information scattered across many months... no help from KU or Bordeaux at that point.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None.. or well: I wrote 100+ emails stressing and it paid off. But I would have been happy without.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not successful. Apparently, you are only allowed courses on the campus you are a part of... I was not told this until late august........ between limitations and keep having to get my forhåndgodkendelse updated as well as my OLA I ended up with mediocre classes I could have been fine without.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Think about it. Just because you are offered a university spot; really think. It has cost me so much money, I have been super stressed from may till late January (since even giving exam dates was hard for Bordeaux to execute) and nothing is worth it. I am happy to be done.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Such a low academic level.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Bachelor level courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Classroom teaching... UCPH is forelæsninger.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Product design, production system management, history of science, basic algorithms and algebra, general mathematics, french

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
French; had Phillip; a great teacher (the best classes of my study)
All the other courses are crazy easy and boring because of it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fine

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: French are closed, don't be abnoxious

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They drink all day

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Wine

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Think about it again, you can drop out
Breathe and remember you are ok
Just because you ask for help does not mean you will get any - you have to deal with 99.99% on your own

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, it's a big mess and you cannot understand until you are in it yourself.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having courses so easy I could focus on myself

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
No communication/coordination/structure/etc from the university or crous.
Everything is on paper in bordeaux - slow on technology
